How does your phone know that puppy and dog mean almost the same thing?
Computers can't read words. So AI turns every word into a list of numbers. That list is called an embedding.
Think of it as a map. Every word gets an address, a spot on that map.
Words with similar meanings land close together. Dog, puppy and wolf cluster. Pizza and pasta live somewhere else.
Nobody placed them by hand. The model learned each spot from which words show up in similar sentences.
Real maps have hundreds or thousands of dimensions, not two. But the rule is the same: distance means meaning.
Even directions carry meaning. Take king, subtract man, add woman, and you land near queen.
That's how search finds what you meant, not just what you typed.
Meaning, turned into geometry. That's the unseen layer under modern AI.
